title: Standard method for microCT-based additive manufacturing quality control
author: Anton Du Plessis
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.4njgvcn

steps.title: Prepare Witness Specimen
steps.instruction: Build a witness specimen in the same process as the complex part. The specimen should be a cylinder with a 15 mm diameter, built vertically to the total height of the complex part.

steps.title: Perform Initial Scan of Complex Part
steps.instruction: Conduct a high-quality microCT scan of the entire complex part to identify general defects and surface imperfections.

substeps.instruction: Load the sample at approximately a 45 degree angle.
Set scanner to 200 kV and 100 µA.
Set image acquisition to 250 ms per image.
Record 3000 images during a 360 degree rotation (without averaging).
Ensure resolution is appropriate for sample width (e.g., 46 µm for the bracket described).

steps.title: Analyze Complex Part Scan
steps.instruction: Process the scan data using VGStudioMax 3.1 to detect internal voids and surface errors.

substeps.instruction: Apply the automatic surface determination function.
Conduct a manual inspection of slice images to confirm findings.

steps.title: Perform High-Resolution Scan of Witness Specimen
steps.instruction: Scan the witness specimen at a higher resolution to visualize thin layered defects.

substeps.instruction: Option 1 (Standard): Load specimen at a 45 degree angle and use identical settings as the complex part scan, but increase resolution (e.g., 20 µm).

Option 2 (High Resolution): Load specimen at a smaller angle, use similar settings but include averaging to improve image quality. Scan at 10 µm resolution by scanning in 4 parts and stitching them together automatically during reconstruction (approx. 2 hours scan time).

steps.title: Analyze Witness Specimen for Layered Defects
steps.instruction: Inspect the witness specimen scan using slice images to reveal layered porosity or stop-start flaws.

steps.title: Perform Optional Zoom Scan of Complex Part
steps.instruction: If defects are found in the witness specimen, perform a high-resolution 'zoom' scan of the corresponding height/location in the complex part.

substeps.instruction: Identify potentially problematic areas based on build height and part orientation.
Scan the specific area at a higher resolution (e.g., 23 µm).
